script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. AUSTIN STREET - DAY

(A busy street in Austin, Texas. People move around, laughing and chatting. The sun shines on their faces.)

NARRATOR (voiceover)
(Soft, introspective)
Austin, Texas. A city of second chances.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

(A quaint coffee shop with wooden tables and mismatched chairs. Customers engage in quiet conversations over steaming mugs. A bell dings as the door opens.)

WAITRESS (smiling)
(to a man in his mid-forties entering)
Welcome back, Mr. Foster. It's good to see you again.

JASON FOSTER (mid-40s, disheveled, weary)
(smiling wearily)
Thanks, Karen. It's good to be back.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LATER

(Jason sits at a table, nursing a cup of coffee. He looks around at the familiar faces, a faraway look in his eyes. The bell dings again as a woman enters.)

NARRATOR (voiceover)
(Soft, hopeful)
And sometimes, those second chances come in the most unexpected ways.

ELLA HARRIS (early 30s, stylish, determined)
(pauses when she sees Jason, her eyes widening slightly)
Jason Foster?

JASON
(surprised, then a small smile)
Ella Harris?

ELLA
(excitedly)
My God, Jason! It's been, what, ten years?

JASON
(nods)
Yes. A long time. How have you been?

ELLA
(smiling)
I'm good. I've been good. Married, two kids. Life's been good to me. But... you looked so different in the newspaper photo when I saw you last.

JASON
(laughs)
A little older, a little grayer.

ELLA
(smiling)
A lot grayer. But you still have that smile.

JASON
(smiling back)
I try.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LATER

(Jason and Ella sit across from each other, chatting easily. They laugh and reminisce about old times.)

ELLA
(looking thoughtful)
I'm glad we ran into each other like this, Jason. I've always wondered what could have been.

JASON
(softly)
Me too, Ella. Me too.

INT. JASON'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

(Jason sits on his couch, staring at an old photograph of him and Ella. The phone rings.)

JASON
(answering)
Hello?

ELLA (voiceover)
(on the phone)
Hi, Jason. It's Ella. I couldn't stop thinking about you after we met today. Would you like to have dinner with me tomorrow night?

JASON
(smiling)
Yes, Ella. I'd like that.

INT. ITALIAN RESTAURANT - NIGHT

(Jason and Ella sit in a cozy Italian restaurant, laughing and enjoying each other's company. The candles flicker on the table, casting warm light on their faces.)

ELLA
(looking at Jason)
It's so good to be here with you again, Jason.

JASON
(smiling)
I feel the same way, Ella.

INT. JASON'S APARTMENT - MORNING

(The sun rises over Austin as Jason wakes up, feeling more alive than he has in years. He looks over at Ella, who sleeps peacefully next to him. He smiles.)

JASON
(whispering)
Second chances.

FADE OUT.

THE END
